P13n1: Now, the Zapatistas also don't prove my whole economic path, from unpriced internal necessities, to a common purse, to getting rid of outside money. Do their communities use collective work to support their schools and clinics, and their autonomous government and resistance? Yes. But they also sell products and trade, and they get outside support. So what do they show? That major necessities and public functions can come out of ordinary market purchase and be governed collectively instead. Outside help can make a community more capable, sure. But if the specialist or the donor or the organization stays indispensable, it can also create gatekeepers and uneven dependence.
